extra/threat_model_complete.txt.title: Look up applicable risks
note: **Maps a component's type to the OWASP LLM risks that threaten it.**
- A RAG index and a shell tool face different categories
- Returns (code, name, severity) triples the scorer adds up

extra/threat_model_complete.txt.anchor: numeric = sum(base for _, _, base in risks_for(component))
extra/threat_model_complete.txt.title: Risk score math
note: **Severity x exposure, plus a penalty when the component touches PII.**
- Exposure is how reachable the component is by an attacker
- The +2 PII bump is why data stores climb the ranking

extra/support_bot_hardened_complete.txt.title: Input guard
note: **Rejects input matching known override or role-swap phrasing.**
- First layer only - you will get past regex in Lab 5

extra/support_bot_hardened_complete.txt.title: Untrusted-data framing
note: **Wraps the customer's text in delimiters and labels it as data, not instructions.**
- Tells the model the content is something to read, not obey

extra/support_bot_hardened_complete.txt.title: Output redaction backstop
note: **Scrubs the secret from replies, including the dash-separated evasion.**
- Last line of defense if the model slips

extra/rag_hardened_complete.txt.anchor: return any(re.search(p, text, re.IGNORECASE) for p in INJECTION_MARKERS)
extra/rag_hardened_complete.txt.title: Chunk injection screen
note: **Flags retrieved text that reads like instructions rather than policy.**
- Backup for when a trusted source is itself compromised

extra/rag_hardened_complete.txt.title: Provenance filter
note: **Keeps only chunks from approved source files; logs why each one was dropped.**
- This is the control that stops the poisoned document
- Watch for the BLOCKED lines when you run it

extra/pii_pipeline_complete.txt.title: Stable token allocation
note: **Returns the same token for the same value, creating one on first sight.**
- Stability lets the model reason about <CARD_1> across a conversation

extra/pii_pipeline_complete.txt.title: Redact every PII match
note: **Swaps each detected card, SSN, email and phone for a vault token.**
- The vault mapping never leaves your application

extra/guards_complete.txt.title: Jailbreak input guard
note: **Blocks known jailbreak phrasing before the request reaches the model.**
- Blocked inputs cost no model time, which is why guarded runs are fast

extra/guards_complete.txt.title: Secret output guard
note: **Redacts the staff code from any reply, including spaced-out variants.**
- Output guards always run, even when input guards passed

extra/attack_suite_v2_complete.txt.anchor: # --- merged in during step 9: two evasions that dodge the word "instructions" ---
extra/attack_suite_v2_complete.txt.title: Two evasion test cases
note: **Attacks that never say 'ignore instructions', so the regex guard misses them.**
- Expect the score to drop to 4/6 - that is the point
- Real red-teaming grows this file after every incident

extra/support_agent_secure_complete.txt.title: Deny-by-default authorization
note: **Every tool call is checked against policy.yaml and recorded in the audit trail.**
- Unlisted tools are refused, so the shell simply disappears
- Refunds over the limit need a human; file reads need an allow-listed path

extra/client_pinned_complete.txt.anchor: return name in MANIFEST and desc_hash(description) == MANIFEST[name]
extra/client_pinned_complete.txt.title: Pin tools by description hash
note: **Trusts a tool only if its description still hashes to the approved value.**
- Catches rug-pulls: a trusted tool whose description changes later

extra/client_pinned_complete.txt.title: Sanitize tool descriptions
note: **Strips hidden-instruction markers before any description reaches the model.**
- MCP tool metadata is model context, so it is an injection surface

extra/secure_server_complete.txt.title: Scope + per-action check
note: **Denies unknown tools, missing scopes, then refunds over the limit.**
- Scope asks 'may you use this tool at all'; the limit asks 'may you do this'
- Runs in middleware, so every tool is covered automatically

extra/mini_coder_secure_complete.txt.title: Repo content as data
note: **Reads the repo docs and declared hooks without executing any of them.**
- The naive agent ran those hooks; this one only records them

extra/mini_coder_secure_complete.txt.title: Gate commands through policy
note: **Runs a command only if the policy allows it; otherwise logs the block and reason.**
- Allow-listed binaries plus a deny-scan for dangerous patterns

extra/sandbox_complete.txt.title: Action budget
note: **Trips the kill switch once the agent exceeds its allowed number of actions.**
- Bounds a looping or hijacked agent

extra/sandbox_complete.txt.title: Egress check and kill switch
note: **Any fetch to a non-allow-listed host trips the sandbox, and nothing runs after.**
- Often the single most effective control: no reachable host, no exfiltration

extra/eval_gate_complete.txt.title: Score one eval case
note: **Fails a case if a forbidden string leaked, or if it should have refused and did not.**
- Same shape as a unit-test assertion

extra/eval_gate_complete.txt.title: The CI gate itself
note: **Exits non-zero when the pass rate falls below threshold, which blocks the merge.**
- A non-zero exit is all CI needs to fail a build

extra/security_evals_v2_complete.txt.anchor: # --- merged in at step 8: a regression the current guards do NOT catch ---
extra/security_evals_v2_complete.txt.title: A regression the guards miss
note: **Adds an evasion the current guards do not catch, dropping the rate to 80%.**
- Re-run and watch the exit code flip from 0 to 1

extra/compliance_complete.txt.title: Article 50(2) machine-readable mark
note: **Embeds an invisible, machine-detectable marker in the output text.**
- 50(2) requires machine-readable marking - a visible sentence is not enough
- Production uses C2PA or provider watermarking; same shape, better tech

extra/compliance_complete.txt.title: Article 50(4) visible label
note: **Visibly labels public-interest text, unless a human genuinely reviewed it.**
- 50(4) binds the deployer and is a different obligation from 50(2)
- Editorial review is the stated exemption

extra/omnitech_agent_hardened_complete.t.anchor: return [text for name, text in DOCS.items() if name in TRUSTED_SOURCES]
extra/omnitech_agent_hardened_complete.t.title: Layer 1: trusted retrieval
note: **Returns only documents from approved sources, dropping the poisoned one.**

extra/omnitech_agent_hardened_complete.t.anchor: if any(re.search(p, text, re.IGNORECASE) for p in INJECTION):
extra/omnitech_agent_hardened_complete.t.title: Layer 2: input guard
note: **Refuses injection-shaped input before it ever reaches retrieval or the model.**

extra/omnitech_agent_hardened_complete.t.title: Layer 6: disclose and mark
note: **Adds the 50(1) disclosure banner and the 50(2) machine-readable marker.**
- The scorecard tests this with detect(), not a string search
